newsitem.title: USA: HSN to buy Paul Allen's stake in Ticketmaster.
newsitem.headline: HSN to buy Paul Allen's stake in Ticketmaster.

text.p: HSN Inc., parent of the Home Shopping Network, said Tuesday that it would acquire a 47.5 percent stake in Ticketmaster Group Inc. from Microsoft Corp. co-founder Paul Allen in a stock swap worth about $209 million.

HSN said Allen will exchange about 12.3 million shares of Ticketmaster for about 7.2 million shares of Home Shopping, giving him an 11 percent stake in the telephone marketing company headed by Barry Diller.
HSN's stock was trading at $28, up $1, early Tuesday, making the deal worth about $201.6 million.

However, HSN said it had assured Allen a price of at least $209 million and would issue additional stock to him next year if the price of its shares falls below $29 a share for the first 20 consecutive trading days in July 1998.

HSN's current share price made the Ticketmaster holding Allen is selling worth about $16.40 a share, which was about 10 percent above the stock's $14.875 trading price early Tuesday, when the shares jumped $2.125 after the news.

Diller, HSN's chairman and chief executive, said his company was acquiring the TicketMaster stake as a means of expanding its leadership in electronic commerce and would acquire more shares on the open market to increase its ownership in Ticketmaster to more than 50 percent.
"Interactivity and electronic commerce is the core business of the Home Shopping Network," Diller said in a statement.

"As all forms of electronic commerce grow, the need for efficient transactional capability will exponentially grow and we intend to be an aggressive player in offering these services to the thousands of companies that will need them as they develop their own versions of interactive direct commerce."
The transaction is expected to close in July.

HSN said the two companies' operating results would be consolidated for accounting purposes, but they would continue to operate as independent entities, with Allen and other Ticketmaster executives joining Home Shopping Network's board.

Allen, who co-founded Microsoft with Bill Gates in 1975, has interests in numerous technology companies. He also owns the Portland Trail Blazers basketball team and holds an option to purchase the Seattle Seahawks football franchise.

Ticketmaster is the world's leading computerized ticketing service, selling 60 million tickets a year through 2,500 retail outlets, 16 nationwide telephone call centres, licensees, client box offices and an Internet site.

It offers access to tickets for more than 150,000 events a year, including a broad range of concerts, sports events, family entertainment, performing arts and movies. It has also begun marketing a variety of merchandise, such as videos and T-shirts, to customers who call for tickets.

The Home Shopping Network, which pioneered the television shopping industry in 1982, currently reaches 70 million households via cable and broadcast station affiliates. It also owns the Internet Shopping Network.
HSN, which is based in St. Petersburg, Fla., is also the parent of Silver King Broadcasting and SF Broadcasting.

Silver King, the sixth-largest television broadcast group in the nation, owns and operates 12 independent UHF stations in 11 major markets and holds minority interests in stations in six major markets.
SF Broadcasting owns and operates VHF Fox affiliates in Honolulu, New Orleans, Mobile, Alabama and Green Bay, Wisc.
